aria: Animated recap of the Magic's 107 to 100 road win at Sacramento: Franz Wagner's 3-pointer with 3:10 left in the second quarter that made it 52 to 43, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his season-high 33 points, the top scorers, how the Magic won, and the next game at Utah.
notes: Box score from the Magic's 107–100 road win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center on Nov 10, 2026, from the Sportradar box score (via the site's sports feed) and the CBS Sports box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sacramento, ABC News and iNFOnews), Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker) and Sports Radio Service. The quarter scores add up to both totals (57–52 at the half and 84–76 after three, matching Sports Radio Service). All 100 Kings points are accounted for in the feed's box score; it lists 100 of Orlando's 107, so 7 Magic points came from players it doesn't list, which doesn't change the top four scorers. Team totals (points in the paint, turnovers, rebounds, threes, bench points, points off turnovers) are from the same box score; the 48–34 rebounding edge counts player rebounds, as the CBS Sports box score does. The Magic's 14-point lead is from the box score and Ball Exclusives; the Kings' 5-point lead is the box score's. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games: Orlando 3–7 and 11th in the East, Sacramento 1–10, Utah 1–10.

Wagner's 33 points were a season high, with 7 rebounds, 7 assists and 10 of 10 free throws (AP, box score). The written recaps and box scores differ on his field goals (AP: 10 of 21; box scores: 11 of 23), so the recap doesn't show that number. Anthony Black had 26 points, 7 rebounds, 5 assists and 4 steals (AP). Sacramento went on an 18–0 run across the first and second quarters to lead 38–34 (box score, Sports Radio Service). The Kings got within 103–98 late before Orlando closed it out (Sports Radio Service). Orlando snapped a four-game losing streak; Sacramento has lost four straight and is 0–6 at home (AP). Paolo Banchero missed his eighth straight game with a high ankle sprain; Jalen Suggs, Jonathan Isaac and Tristan da Silva didn't play (AP). Orlando plays at Utah on Wednesday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Wagner's 3-pointer with 3:10 left in the second quarter, which capped an 18–5 run and made it 52–43; the Magic led the rest of the way (AP). It was his only three in 5 attempts (box score). The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Orlando Magic or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Wagner's listed 6-foot-10 and 220 pounds (RealGM); no wingspan is reported, so his arms use standard proportions. He is in Orlando's road kit with No. 22 (AP photo captions). He isn't in the star-look file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
